status: Production storyboards; replacement footage, final voice and music not yet produced or approved.

films.title: The work. The evidence. The impact.
films.goal: Explain one complete work-to-report journey in 75 seconds.
films.music: 100 BPM; warm electronic pulse, rounded bass, restrained percussion. Introduce rhythm after the opening question.
films.proof: One completed synthetic work item appears once in Records and is selected as a report source.

shots.picture: Tight crop of a finished, source-linked report. Cut to three separate task, spreadsheet and note fragments. Overlay: Where did the impact go?
shots.voice: The work gets done. But when someone asks what changed, the story is scattered across spreadsheets, inboxes, and memory.
shots.edit: Cold open; three clean cuts; no logo bumper. One muted paper sound, then a beat of silence.

shots.picture: Pull back into the real VANTAGE workspace. Show one synthetic work item with an owner, context and status.
shots.voice: VANTAGE brings that story together. It connects daily work, performance records, and reporting in a workspace built for Marines and operational teams.
shots.edit: J-cut: start the sentence before the UI appears. Flat logo in the app; persistent Demo data label.

shots.picture: Complete the selected item through its actual workflow. Hold the confirmation, then open its resulting record.
shots.voice: Start with the work. Capture the outcome, the amount, and the supporting context. Check what you are saving, then keep it with the record.
shots.edit: Follow one cursor. Punch in only on outcome fields. Do not cut across the save and confirmation.

shots.picture: Show the outcome in its correct metric group; open the source detail. Keep UMT counts separate from unrelated units.
shots.voice: The picture grows from those records. You can see what was accomplished and inspect the detail behind it, without treating every entry as the same kind of output.
shots.edit: Match cut on the identical item title. Teal underline on the source link. Hold the evidence for three seconds.

shots.picture: Open Reports, choose the relevant range and records, generate a draft, open a source, revise one sentence and save.
shots.voice: When it is time to report, start from the evidence you already have. Build a draft, check its sources, and edit it before you share it. The judgment stays with you.
shots.edit: Compress genuine loading with a visible Time shortened label. Music drops under source explanation. No simulated AI response.

shots.picture: Full product frame, then flat mark and short end line: Make the work visible. CTA: Explore VANTAGE.
shots.voice: VANTAGE. Make the work visible, keep the evidence close, and turn everyday action into a clearer picture. Explore the product to see how it works.
shots.edit: Resolve the musical phrase. Two-second end-card hold, clean audio tail, no trailer boom.

films.title: Your first week in VANTAGE
films.goal: Establish a small repeatable routine rather than tour every menu.
films.music: 92 BPM; soft keys and sparse pulse. Lower energy than the overview.
films.proof: User can save a record, correct it, create a measurable goal and review a weekly report selection.

shots.picture: Open on a populated weekly record list. Overlay: A useful first week.
shots.voice: Your first week has one goal: build a record you can actually use. Start small, and keep the detail while it is fresh.
shots.edit: Outcome first. Gentle 110% crop; music enters beneath the second sentence.

shots.picture: Day one: show profile, rank, unit membership and record visibility controls using a fictional account.
shots.voice: Check your profile and unit membership first. Review the visibility setting whenever you create a record. Your role and membership determine which team views you can access.
shots.edit: Day 1 chapter marker. Circle only the control being explained. Never show a password or invitation token.

shots.picture: Open Quick Log. Enter a synthetic completed task, review the parsed fields, choose visibility and save.
shots.voice: Log one real outcome from your day. Include what you did, how much you completed, and why it mattered. Review the fields and save the activity.
shots.edit: Typing accelerated between the first and last words; normal-speed review and save. Show confirmation.

shots.picture: Day two: reopen the record and correct a result. Open Goals and set one measurable target with the correct unit.
shots.voice: If you missed context, edit the record. Then choose one measurable goal. Use a target with a clear unit, so progress tells you something useful.
shots.edit: Cut on navigation. Before-and-after text highlight; preserve the rest of the screen.

shots.picture: Friday: filter the reporting period and inspect the recorded work. Open a report source.
shots.voice: At the end of the week, review your records for missing detail and check the reporting period. Open the source behind a figure before relying on it.
shots.edit: Friday chapter marker. No fictional time-saving counter. Let the viewer read the date range.

shots.picture: Three-line recap: Capture / Check / Review. End on Quick Log entry point.
shots.voice: Capture while the detail is fresh. Check what you saved. Review the week. That is enough to make your first week useful.
shots.edit: Three beat-synced reveals; fade music over the last two seconds.

films.title: From one sentence to a saved record
films.goal: Show successful capture, review, save and retrieval.
films.music: 96 BPM; minimal plucked synth and quiet pulse.
films.proof: Save activity succeeds; the saved record preserves quantity, amount, value type, date and visibility.

shots.picture: Close-up of the finished record: 8 UMTs, $12,600, result and date. Overlay: Start with one sentence.
shots.voice: A useful record starts with what you actually did. Here is how to capture it without losing the detail.
shots.edit: Result-first cold open; one short confirmation sound.

shots.picture: Return to Today; activate Quick Log through the visible control. Show N shortcut as optional annotation.
shots.voice: Open Quick Log from the workspace. You can also press N when you are not typing into another field.
shots.edit: Cursor glide to the real button. Tiny N callout outside the click target.

shots.picture: Type: Resolved 8 UMTs totaling $12,600 yesterday. Show parsing finish before the next shot.
shots.voice: Write a clear sentence. Include the action, quantity, amount, and date. VANTAGE proposes structured fields from the text for you to review.
shots.edit: Speed up typing only. Keep the final sentence visible for three seconds.

shots.picture: Open details. Inspect count, unit, amount, value type and date; choose visibility and fix one field if needed.
shots.voice: Check the quantity and dollar amount separately. Confirm the type of financial action and the date, then choose who should see the record. Correct anything the parser misunderstood.
shots.edit: Two restrained punch-ins. Use a labeled illustrative example; never call all reviewed dollars savings.

shots.picture: Click Save activity. Keep success feedback visible. Open Records and the newly saved item.
shots.voice: Save the activity, then open it in Records. You should see the same outcome and the details you just checked.
shots.edit: Unbroken save-to-confirmation shot. Match cut to identical saved title; music ducks.

shots.picture: Hold the saved record. End overlay: Capture. Review. Save.
shots.voice: One sentence starts the record. Your review makes it useful.
shots.edit: No Escape-to-discard ending. Two-second end hold with captions still visible.

films.title: Choose who can see the record
films.goal: Demonstrate private and shared records with two different roles.
films.music: 84 BPM; quiet ambient bed, no dramatic security effects.
films.proof: A member and a separate leader account show the intended record visible only after sharing; audit view verified before narration.

shots.picture: Two labeled views: My record / Leader view. Shared record is not present in the leader view yet.
shots.voice: Before you share a record, know which audience you are choosing. Visibility is a decision worth checking at the point of saving.
shots.edit: Split screen only for role comparison. Both panels labeled Demo accounts.

shots.picture: Open record details and show the actual selected visibility, not a decorative privacy badge.
shots.voice: Open the record and inspect its visibility. Do not assume a default: check the setting on the record you are about to use.
shots.edit: Slow 120% crop to visibility control. Music remains low.

shots.picture: Save a private test record. Switch to a separate ordinary unit leader session and inspect the corresponding view.
shots.voice: In this example, the record is private. The ordinary unit leader view does not include it. These two screens belong to different test users.
shots.edit: Role title card during switch; do not log in as owner for the leader example.

shots.picture: Return to the member; share to the intended unit; save; inspect the named unit before confirmation.
shots.voice: When you want to share, select the correct unit and save. Check the unit name as carefully as the visibility setting.
shots.edit: One close-up. Keep save confirmation in frame; discrete tick sound.

shots.picture: Leader opens the now-shared record. Return to the member audit view and locate the actual access event if present.
shots.voice: The shared record is now available to the authorized leader. Review the access history available in your deployment to understand how it was used.
shots.edit: Match cut on exact record title. Do not claim universal access logging if this event is absent.

shots.picture: End on the record visibility control with recap: Check audience / Check unit / Save.
shots.voice: Choose the audience, confirm the unit, and check the saved result.
shots.edit: No claims about absolute privacy from system administrators. Resolve gently.

films.title: Bring a spreadsheet into the work queue
films.goal: Teach preview, validation, apply and identical-file reimport.
films.music: 96 BPM; light pulse, remove percussion during validation.
films.proof: Preview counts match applied rows; invalid input is handled visibly; identical reimport demonstrates its actual no-change result.

shots.picture: Show a small completed queue and its original synthetic workbook. Overlay: Keep the source.
shots.voice: Your spreadsheet already contains useful work. Bring it into VANTAGE with the source and the review steps intact.
shots.edit: Match cut from original workbook to the queue. No confidential files.

shots.picture: Work > Queue > Import a spreadsheet. Select a five-row fixture containing one intentional validation issue.
shots.voice: Open the queue and choose Import a spreadsheet. Select your file, then review the sheet and fields VANTAGE will use.
shots.edit: Chapter Upload. Crop to file selection result; omit filesystem paths and unrelated filenames.

shots.picture: Show sheet selection, headers and field mapping. Point at row identity and financial fields.
shots.voice: Match the fields carefully. Check the identifiers, amounts, and units. A preview is the time to catch a column that would otherwise mean something different.
shots.edit: Chapter Map. Normal speed on mapping changes. Teal highlight on one column at a time.

shots.picture: Inspect the validation issue, correct the fixture or mapping, rerun preview and verify every displayed count.
shots.voice: Read the validation message before applying anything. Correct the issue and preview again. The counts and sample rows should match what you intend to bring in.
shots.edit: Chapter Review. Show the real error and recovery. No cut that makes the bad row disappear without explanation.

shots.picture: Apply the import; show its result and open one created work item plus its original source.
shots.voice: Apply the reviewed import. Open a work item and inspect its source so you can confirm where the row came from.
shots.edit: Keep apply and success intact. Pause on provenance; two-second music dip.

shots.picture: Import the unchanged file again. Show actual unchanged result. End with queue and source together.
shots.voice: Reimport the same unchanged file and inspect the result. This example should produce no duplicate work. A changed file is a different case and deserves another review.
shots.edit: Chapter Reimport. Show real unchanged counts; do not imply every modified workbook is idempotent.

films.title: Claim the work. Close the loop.
films.goal: Demonstrate ownership, status, resolution and one linked activity.
films.music: 102 BPM; soft rhythmic ticks, purposeful forward motion.
films.proof: Item claim and resolution succeed; the linked activity exists once; an unchanged repeat does not add a second outcome.

shots.picture: Open on resolved work item beside its linked activity. Overlay: One outcome, connected.
shots.voice: Finishing the task is only part of the job. Keep who did it, what changed, and the record of the outcome together.
shots.edit: Outcome-first split composition, then return to full product.

shots.picture: Open Work > Queue. Filter unclaimed items; inspect one row before claiming it.
shots.voice: Start in the queue. Find an available item, open its detail, and read the source before taking ownership.
shots.edit: Show the actual filter selected. No frantic scrolling.

shots.picture: Claim the item and show the owner field. Briefly demonstrate already-claimed state from the second test account.
shots.voice: Claim the item so the team can see who is working it. If someone already owns it, resolve that handoff before proceeding.
shots.edit: Cursor spotlight on claim; hold owner confirmation. Role switch explicitly labeled.

shots.picture: Update state and record follow-up context or supporting file through existing controls.
shots.voice: As the work moves, update its state and preserve useful context. Someone opening it later should understand what happened and what still needs attention.
shots.edit: Match cuts within the same item. One soft click accent on meaningful state change.

shots.picture: Resolve the item using actual completion controls. Show captured quantity, financial type and result, then open linked activity.
shots.voice: When the work is complete, record the outcome accurately. Check the amount and action type, then inspect the activity connected to the completed item.
shots.edit: Do not skip confirmation. Hold completed state and linked record for four seconds.

shots.picture: Return to queue and show the item in completed view. Overlay: Claim / Update / Resolve.
shots.voice: The queue shows the work is finished, and the record keeps the outcome. That is the loop you want to close.
shots.edit: Three-step recap. No promise of automatic recording until the actual linkage is shown.

films.title: Build a report you can trace
films.audience: Individuals preparing narratives and leaders reviewing them
films.goal: Show source selection, real generation, revision and export.
films.music: 90 BPM; quiet piano or soft synth, slight lift at export.
films.proof: Draft generated using enabled capability; source opens; revision saves; exported document contains the edited text.

shots.picture: Open an actual generated report and its source list. Overlay: Start with evidence.
shots.voice: A convincing report begins with the facts behind it. VANTAGE helps you build the draft while keeping those facts within reach.
shots.edit: Hard cut from headline to real source list; no invented final document.

shots.picture: Reports > Packages. Create or open a package. Set reporting period, output type and relevant source selection.
shots.voice: Open Reports and choose the package you need. Set the reporting period and check which records belong in this draft.
shots.edit: Chapter Select. Hold the full date range, then move to source selection.

shots.picture: Click the actual generation action. Capture true loading and returned result; identify template or connected AI mode accurately.
shots.voice: Generate the draft from the selected material. If your deployment has AI enabled, use the available VANTAGE action and wait for the actual response.
shots.edit: Time-shortened loading may use a labeled cut. If generation fails, show the failure or retake after fixing it.

shots.picture: Open a citation or source link. Compare a figure and sentence to the underlying record.
shots.voice: Check the source behind a figure. The right number still needs the right meaning: reviewed funds, resolved discrepancies, and savings are different kinds of outcomes.
shots.edit: L-cut narration over source detail. Highlight matching text without covering it.

shots.picture: Edit a sentence, save the revision, inspect history if available, then export and open the file.
shots.voice: Edit the draft for accuracy and context. Save the revision, then export it. Open the result and confirm that your changes carried through.
shots.edit: Unbroken save feedback. Cut to actual exported file with synthetic data and no local path visible.

shots.picture: Report and source side by side. Recap: Select / Generate / Check / Edit.
shots.voice: VANTAGE helps assemble the work. You remain responsible for the final words.
shots.edit: Music lift at export, then resolve; no unsupported compliance claim.

films.title: Read the number. Inspect the evidence.
films.goal: Explain scope, units, filters and drill-down without misleading aggregation.
films.music: 86 BPM; sparse ambient plucks; long quiet holds on figures.
films.proof: Visible date range and metric definition match the evidence; unlike units remain distinct.

shots.picture: Large crop: 8 UMTs beside 3 training hours, with the two groups separate.
shots.voice: Eight financial actions and three training hours describe different work. Useful analysis preserves that difference.
shots.edit: Two clean reveals. Never animate the figures into a meaningless total.

shots.picture: Open full analysis through Reports. Show the actual selected reporting period and audience scope.
shots.voice: Begin with the scope. Check the period, the person or unit, and any filters before interpreting the results.
shots.edit: Chapter Scope. Teal bracket on range; normal-speed filter change.

shots.picture: Inspect one quantity group and one financial group. Show category or value-type labels.
shots.voice: Read the unit and the financial action type beside the number. A dollar amount alone does not explain what was accomplished.
shots.edit: Chapter Meaning. Punch in on labels, not only the headline numbers.

shots.picture: Open the record list underlying one displayed metric. Inspect a representative result.
shots.voice: Open the records behind a figure. Check whether the selected work supports the conclusion you were about to draw.
shots.edit: Chapter Evidence. Match cut using the same title and amount. Hold for a silent inspection beat.

shots.picture: Change the period or supported filter; show corresponding evidence set. Include a no-data view if useful.
shots.voice: Change the period and watch the evidence change with it. An empty view tells you there is no matching record here; it does not prove no work happened.
shots.edit: Chapter Compare. Show selected filter throughout; no invented before-and-after performance gains.

shots.picture: End on scope, metric group and source list together. Overlay: Scope / Meaning / Evidence.
shots.voice: Check the scope, understand the unit, and inspect the evidence. Then decide what the number means.
shots.edit: Quiet three-part recap with three seconds to read.

films.title: A clearer picture for the team
films.goal: Show permission-scoped team visibility and practical follow-up.
films.music: 98 BPM; steady pulse with restrained bass.
films.proof: Leader sees intended unit, can inspect a shared source, and cannot see a control record in another unit.

shots.picture: Team overview with a real selected unit and a clear follow-up item.
shots.voice: A team picture should help you decide where to look next, without losing the people and work behind it.
shots.edit: Start on the decision, not a menu fly-through.

shots.picture: Sign into ordinary leader test account and open Team. Hold unit name and membership context.
shots.voice: Open Team with your leadership role. Confirm which unit you are viewing and what your membership allows you to see.
shots.edit: Role label stays visible. Never use the operator account to imply ordinary-leader permissions.

shots.picture: Inspect an available workload or shared-outcome view. Open a synthetic member with shared records.
shots.voice: Use the shared records and available team views to understand the work. Select a person or outcome when you need the supporting detail.
shots.edit: Move from overview to detail with a controlled 250ms transition.

shots.picture: Open a shared record with missing follow-up context; show the source and current state.
shots.voice: Before acting on a summary, open the source. Look for the owner, the status, and the context that explains what still needs attention.
shots.edit: Emphasize the source label and actual state. Music ducks under explanation.

shots.picture: Show the second unit permission control case and an empty/shared-only view.
shots.voice: This view reflects the records and permissions available here. Missing or unshared records are a visibility limit, not a measure of someone’s effort.
shots.edit: Side-by-side only for the scoped comparison. No ranking or leaderboard of fictional personnel.

shots.picture: Return to a useful shared record and recap: Scope / Source / Follow-up.
shots.voice: Confirm the scope, inspect the source, and make the next conversation more informed.
shots.edit: Soft musical resolution, clear end frame.

films.title: Record the conversation. Confirm the acknowledgement.
films.goal: Show both sides of a counseling and the acknowledged-state behavior.
films.music: 80 BPM; warm understated pad and piano, no triumphal accents.
films.proof: Leader creates a counseling; subject acknowledges; acknowledged status persists; edit restrictions are demonstrated.

shots.picture: Counseling detail with date, summary, follow-up and acknowledgement state.
shots.voice: A useful counseling record keeps the conversation, the next steps, and the acknowledgement clear to both people.
shots.edit: No sensitive personnel examples; fictional development discussion only.

shots.picture: Leader opens the authorized member view and begins recording a counseling.
shots.voice: From the authorized member view, record the counseling. Check the Marine, the date, and the type before adding the summary.
shots.edit: Chapter Record. Highlight subject identity; do not expose real personnel.

shots.picture: Fill strengths, improvements, goals and follow-up date with a short synthetic example. Save.
shots.voice: Write specific strengths and improvements, then agree on a measurable next step and follow-up date. Review the record before saving it.
shots.edit: Typing accelerated, review at normal speed. Keep save confirmation.

shots.picture: Switch to the subject’s account. Open the counseling in Career and read the same content.
shots.voice: The Marine opens the counseling and reviews the content. Both views should refer to the same conversation and next steps.
shots.edit: Explicit role-change slate. Match cut on the counseling title and date.

shots.picture: Click Acknowledge as the subject. Reload or reopen to show persisted status; leader inspects restrictions.
shots.voice: Acknowledge after reviewing the record. Confirm the status changed, and check how the acknowledged record can be handled in this deployment.
shots.edit: Keep acknowledgement action and result continuous. Do not call acknowledgement legal agreement or consent.

shots.picture: Hold follow-up date and acknowledged state. Overlay: The next step stays visible.
shots.voice: Keep the follow-up visible so the conversation leads to action.
shots.edit: Calm closing beat. No public individual assessment or ratings.

films.title: Prepare a deployment for its first users
films.goal: Teach first-run sequence and verification without leaking secrets or implying accreditation.
films.music: 88 BPM; minimal steady bed, silence for important verification steps.
films.proof: Synthetic deployment health is verified; first-run locks after setup; member visibility matches configured memberships.

shots.picture: Local synthetic deployment with First-run checklist; verified health screen at end-state preview.
shots.voice: A useful deployment starts with clear ownership and a few deliberate checks before the first users arrive.
shots.edit: Use only disposable staging. No real dashboard billing, keys or production addresses.

shots.picture: Show prepared hosting/configuration checklist: public URL, persistent storage, email choice and backup ownership; values masked.
shots.voice: Confirm the intended public address, persistent storage, and operational responsibilities. Configure the required settings through your deployment’s documented process, keeping secret values out of recordings.
shots.edit: Chapter Prepare. Use a factual checklist, not a fake hosting console. Do not show credential entry.

shots.picture: Show initial owner setup before and after secure credential entry, then verify setup cannot be reused.
shots.voice: Complete the first-run owner setup. Then verify that setup is closed and that the owner can sign in through the intended route.
shots.edit: Cut around secret entry, labeled Credential entry omitted. Preserve genuine before-and-after UI.

shots.picture: Owner creates a small synthetic unit structure and assigns supported roles. Show an unattached member’s limited view.
shots.voice: Define the units and assign roles deliberately. Check a new member before and after attachment so the unit’s information appears only where intended.
shots.edit: Chapter Membership. Role-change slate and controlled comparison. No bulk production mutations.

shots.picture: Owner checks authentication options, email if enabled, backup/restore evidence from staging, and a member walkthrough.
shots.voice: Verify the workflows the deployment relies on: sign-in, membership, saving a record, and reporting. Test backup recovery in staging. A successful homepage is not a complete deployment check.
shots.edit: Chapter Verify. Hold results long enough to inspect; do not narrate a test as passed without its evidence.

shots.picture: Handoff sheet: owner, support route, configuration record, backup responsibility, test date and open items.
shots.voice: Record who owns the deployment and how users get help. Keep a dated configuration and verification record. VANTAGE is independent software; deploying it does not establish official approval.
shots.edit: End on operational handoff, not account secrets. No music swell suggesting certification.

films.title: Understand retention, holds and the inventory
films.goal: Explain available controls and their operational meaning using safe synthetic examples.
films.music: 78 BPM; quiet ambient bed, no percussion during schedule review.
films.proof: Disabled schedule and documented authority shown; hold behavior verified in staging; inventory export opens correctly.

shots.picture: Owner console: retention schedules, hold indicator and inventory export preview.
shots.voice: Governance starts with knowing what is stored, what rules apply, and who is responsible for those decisions.
shots.edit: Three purposeful cuts, no compliance stamp or shield animation.

shots.picture: Open Retention. Inspect a disabled synthetic schedule and the fields for scope and authority.
shots.voice: Review the schedule’s scope and status. Read the stated authority and confirm that it applies before enabling any retention behavior.
shots.edit: Chapter Schedule. Keep status and authority visible together. No real authority invented for the example.

shots.picture: Open a held synthetic record and its actual hold information. Show documented staging verification result.
shots.voice: A hold changes how the affected records should be handled. Verify the behavior in a disposable environment rather than assuming a label is enough.
shots.edit: Chapter Hold. No live purge or destructive action. A verified fixture may demonstrate the blocked outcome.

shots.picture: Open Privacy inventory. Read actual categories, counts and any disclosed gaps.
shots.voice: Open the inventory and inspect what it reports. Read its gaps as well as its totals. The inventory is an input to review, not a substitute for one.
shots.edit: Chapter Inventory. Slow pan only if needed. Do not expose personal records beneath aggregate counts.

shots.picture: Export inventory as Markdown and open the real file. Compare one label and count with the source screen.
shots.voice: Export the inventory and compare it with the screen. Keep the date and deployment context so another reviewer knows what the document describes.
shots.edit: Chapter Export. Match cut on the same category. Keep local paths hidden.

shots.picture: End on three short lines: Scope / Authority / Verification, with independent-software clarification.
shots.voice: Decide the scope, document the authority, and verify the behavior. These controls support your process; they do not confer approval or compliance by themselves.
shots.edit: Fade to flat mark; measured delivery, no dramatic closing effect.
